name: Buttermilk Drop Biscuits With Garlic and Cheddar

instructions.primary_message: Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and preheat to 200°C (400°F). Sift flour into a large bowl. If using butter, dice into 0.5-cm pieces, then toss with flour and rub with your fingertips until no visible bits remain. Whisk in parsley or chives, baking powder, sugar, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and cayenne. Add the finely grated cheddar, and toss until well combined. Pour in buttermilk, and stir with a flexible spatula to form a soft dough.

With a pair of spoons, drop the dough into 10 large portions on a parchment-lined half sheet pan (it's fine to eyeball their size; no need to weigh). Bake until golden brown all over, about 25 minutes. Cool 5 minutes and serve—the flavor of the biscuits will intensify as they cool. In an airtight container, leftovers will keep up to 24 hours at room temperature; warm in a hot oven to serve.

schema_metadata.keywords: baking, biscuit, buttermilk, cheddar, cheese, drop biscuit, garlic

description: Garlicky and cheesy buttermilk drop biscuits that go with any meal. The best part? The dry mix can be prepared far in advance.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 28 g unsalted butter (2 tablespoons; 30 g) (optional)

Optional substitutions: fresh parsley → chives

Notes: The consistency of these biscuits, and even their yield, depends on using a fine, Microplane or Parmesan-style grater for the cheese. I love Microplane's fine grater because it's extra wide, and makes quick work of the cheese.
author: Stella Parks
